articles.title: Trump pressiona Brasil para influenciar eleições, diz professor | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao podcast O Assunto, professor da FGV e pesquisador do Carnegie Endowment Oliver Stuenkel afirma que pressão dos EUA sobre Brasil segue padrão já aplicado a Argentina, Honduras e outros países.
articles.summary: Oliver Stuenkel analisa como Trump pressiona o Brasil para influenciar as eleições na América Latina, seguindo um padrão de interferência política e comercial na região.
articles.body:
O governo de Donald Trump tem ampliado a pressão sobre processos políticos e eleitorais de outros países, e o caso brasileiro faz parte dessa estratégia . A avaliação é do professor de Relações Internacionais da FGV e pesquisador do Carnegie Endowment Oliver Stuenkel, em entrevista ao podcast "O Assunto".

A análise ocorre na discussão sobre a lista de 52 exigências enviada pelos Estados Unidos ao Brasil nas negociações para tentar reverter o tarifaço. Entre os itens estava a garantia de que "dissidentes políticos" pudessem disputar as eleições de 2026.

A informação foi revelada pelo jornal "O Estado de S. Paulo" e confirmada pela GloboNews com fontes da diplomacia nesta quinta-feira (17). O governo brasileiro rejeitou essa e outras propostas e afirmou que questões políticas, judiciais e de soberania não estariam na mesa de negociação.

Para Stuenkel, o documento mostra que a política tarifária americana foi usada com objetivos que vão além do comércio.

"O governo Trump utiliza tarifas para atingir metas em áreas não relacionadas ao comércio, utiliza tarifas como ferramenta política", disse. Segundo ele, o texto enviado ao Brasil "explicita claramente o desejo por parte dos Estados Unidos de interferir em assuntos internos".

O professor avalia que o episódio não é isolado. "O que estamos vendo no caso brasileiro faz parte de um projeto que se aplica a toda a América Latina", afirmou. O que chama atenção, na avaliação dele, é o quanto essas ameaças são explícitas, algo pouco comum nesse tipo de relação.

Stuenkel cita dois casos de pressão americana sobre disputas eleitorais na região. Na Argentina, Trump manifestou preferência por um dos lados durante a eleição legislativa do ano passado e afirmou que a ajuda dos Estados Unidos ao país poderia não durar tanto tempo caso o grupo político adversário de Milei vencesse.

O professor disse ter estado no país naquele momento e avaliou que o apoio americano provavelmente teve algum impacto para melhorar o resultado do atual presidente argentino, num cenário em que a moeda local estava fragilizada .

O segundo caso é Honduras. Segundo o professor, Trump ameaçou uma grave crise na relação bilateral caso seu candidato preferido, Nasry Asfura, não fosse eleito. Por se tratar de um país bastante dependente dos Estados Unidos, ele avalia que a declaração também pode ter tido efeito sobre o eleitorado.

Foto de arquivo: Trump mostra tabela do tarifaço em 2 de abril de 2025 — Foto: Reuters/Carlos Barria/File Photo

Stuenkel afirma que a pressão americana não se restringe a períodos eleitorais e atinge decisões internas de outros países. Ele mencionou o Peru, pressionado a excluir atores chineses do controle de um porto estratégico, e o Panamá, pressionado a expulsar empresas chinesas que operam portos no canal . "Da mesma forma, pressionam o Brasil a fazer certas mudanças na política interna", disse.

O professor acrescenta que essa movimentação é feita com a expectativa de que nem tudo funcione. "Existe uma percepção aqui em Washington de que o governo Trump tenta algumas coisas e vê o que cola", afirmou o pesquisador, que está na capital americana.

Segundo ele, há também a percepção de que o Brasil, por ser um país maior, não necessariamente aceitará todas as demandas, mesmo sendo ameaçado.

Fora da América Latina, Stuenkel citou Alemanha, Austrália e Canadá. No caso alemão, o vice-presidente J.D. Vance esteve no país pouco antes das eleições e deixou clara a preferência do governo americano pelo AfD, partido de extrema direita.

Na Austrália e no Canadá, avalia o professor, a pressão surtiu efeito contrário, e os candidatos alinhados a Trump foram prejudicados eleitoralmente. Segundo ele, os eleitores desses países se sentiram ameaçados e passaram a ver a integridade e a soberania nacionais sob risco.

Esse tipo de atuação pública tem sido, para Stuenkel, a estratégia dominante do governo americano até aqui. Ele fez a ressalva de que isso vale "por enquanto" e que não há garantia de que outras estratégias não venham a ser usadas no futuro.

articles.title: Anthropic quietly sets up biology lab for AI drug project
articles.summary: US News: SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic has set up a wet lab in San Francisco Bay Area, expanding its artificial intelligence ambitions into physical biology and dru.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO: Anthropic has set up a wet lab in San Francisco Bay Area, expanding its artificial intelligence ambitions into physical biology and drug science, according to two people familiar with the matter and company life sciences head Eric Kauderer-Abrams.The Dario Amodei-led startup has said it wants to unlock treatments for rare diseases, taking its biology work beyond computer evaluations. A spokesperson said the lab was not specifically for drug discovery but declined to elaborate. "We believe that to do biology, the final test is still and will be for a while in real lab work," Kauderer-Abrams said. He said Anthropic conducted some work in its facilities and some with external partners.Anthropic wants its Claude AI to direct robotic units conducting experiments with limited human intervention, a source said. Its spokesperson said human involvement remained essential for safety."In our life-science work, we're always balancing these things," Kauderer-Abrams said, "making models better in ways that we think will uplift and accelerate developing medicines, and being thoughtful about how we deploy it to limit the risk."Anthropic said in June it planned preclinical work in areas traditional companies found financially unattractive. It launched Claude Science, added Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan to its board and acquired Coefficient Bio for about $400 million in stock, according to media reports. Anthropic confirmed the acquisition but not the price.The company is expanding in-house laboratory work for speed and firsthand biology experience, while outsourcing where efficient. Job advertisements indicate it is hiring for procurement and operations as well as protein and nucleic acid characterisation. Life sciences is already among its biggest investment areas by staff.Anthropic believes AI could accelerate work on previously "undruggable" conditions, including development of complex antibodies. However, the diseases targeted and its progress remain unclear. It is not conducting clinical trials for now, focusing on needs industry would not address. The toll is likely to rise as many of the injured were reported to be critical.No group officially claimed the attack till late Friday though the role of Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), an umbrella militant alliance formed by three armed groups operating in the region, is alleged. Three to five gunmen besides the driver of the car laden with explosives are suspected to have participated in the attack and were seen attempting to enter the police compound while exchanging fire. The car exploded after ramming into the mosque's entrance wall. articles.summary: US News: The US State Department has approved a possible $2.68 billion military sale to Ukraine for air-defence development upgrades, equipment and related ser.
articles.body: The US State Department has approved a possible $2.68 billion military sale to Ukraine for air-defence development upgrades, equipment and related services, as Kyiv faces continued Russian attacks and seeks stronger security support from its allies.The department announced the determination late on Friday, describing the package as focused on upgrading Ukraine’s air-defence capabilities. The proposed sale comes as US-mediated efforts to end Russia’s more than four-year full-scale invasion have stalled, with territorial concessions in eastern Ukraine remaining a key sticking point in negotiations.Ukraine has also been seeking security guarantees from its partners as part of any potential settlement.The announcement came as Russian forces continued attacks across Ukraine. Two people were killed and two others injured in overnight strikes in the Zhytomyr region, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service. The strikes triggered fires at warehouse and production buildings, while repeated air raid alerts disrupted rescue operations.In the Kharkiv region, one person was killed and six injured after a Russian drone struck an electric train at a railway station in the Novovodolazka community. The attack set two carriages on fire. Another Russian drone attack destroyed a shopping complex in Zaporizhzhia and injured one person.Russia’s Defence Ministry also said its forces struck Ukrainian ports, vessels and a military logistics centre. It said a bulk carrier was hit at the port of Chornomorsk and that a Nova Poshta logistics facility near Odesa, allegedly used to store and distribute military cargo from Europe, was targeted.The ministry separately said Russian air defences intercepted and destroyed 629 Ukrainian drones overnight across 14 Russian regions, Crimea and areas around the Azov and Black seas. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 350 drones were headed towards the Russian capital, with 64 reportedly downed as they approached the city.The US arms approval also comes as Ukraine receives additional European financial support. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv had received a 3.3 billion-euro tranche, worth roughly $3.8 billion, from an EU support package intended to strengthen defence capabilities, including through the purchase of missiles and drones.Zelenskyy made the remarks as Ukraine hosted the inaugural “Carpathian Eight” summit in western Ukraine, bringing together regional leaders to discuss security, energy, logistics and economic cooperation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Almost started a war': How an AI error led to a close call between US and China
articles.summary: US News: An intelligence report circulated across the US military this spring during the war with Iran set off an alarming chain of events after it claimed tha.
articles.body: An intelligence report circulated across the US military this spring during the war with Iran set off an alarming chain of events after it claimed that a Chinese ship in the Middle East was carrying components linked to a nuclear weapons programme.According to CNN, the report prompted the US military to prepare an operation to intercept the vessel. Armed US personnel were preparing to board the ship, while military aircraft were already in the air, according to sources familiar with the episode. It was only shortly before the planned operation that officials took a closer look at the intelligence and discovered that it had been produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence.The chatbot used by a US Special Operations Command analyst had incorrectly identified the material listed in the ship's manifest. The resulting intelligence report, described by one source as "entirely false", had travelled through official channels and was being treated as credible military intelligence. "It almost started a war," the source told CNN.AI error reaches military chainThe incident began when the analyst examined intelligence about the ship's manifest that originated with US Special Operations Command Pacific, based in Hawaii. The analyst queried a chatbot about the information, but the AI system incorrectly identified the cargo.The chatbot had combined open-source information with classified signals intelligence held by the US government before reaching its conclusion. The analyst then used AI again to turn the findings into a standard intelligence report, giving the information the format and appearance of conventional military intelligence before it was disseminated.CNN reported that it could not establish whether the chatbot was a commercially available system or an AI tool developed for the US government. A former senior US official familiar with the systems used by military and intelligence analysts told CNN that internal tools were "mostly just copies of the commercial stuff wearing lipstick".The episode highlights the risks of relying on AI-generated analysis in situations where decisions have to be made rapidly and the consequences of an error can extend beyond the battlefield. Any US attempt to board or otherwise confront a Chinese vessel could have risked escalating into a broader confrontation between Washington and Beijing.US military and intelligence agencies are nevertheless rapidly expanding their use of AI. The technology is being explored for analysing huge volumes of intelligence, selecting targets, moving military assets and handling logistics, budgeting and supply chains. Defence officials have argued that faster AI-assisted decision-making could be critical in a future conflict with China or another major adversary.In January, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth released the Pentagon's "Artificial Intelligence Acceleration Strategy", aimed at speeding up the military's adoption of AI.From battlefield intelligence to weaponsThe episode comes as governments, militaries and AI companies grapple with another question: how increasingly capable AI systems can be prevented from being misused for military purposes.Anthropic recently reported that a Yemen-based weapons engineering cell had used its Claude AI model to develop guidance, navigation and control software for missiles and a guided rocket. The company said the group used Claude Code in place of human software engineers to integrate an open-source autopilot with a phone-class flight computer, write control software, tune settings, run firmware builds and conduct flight simulations.Anthropic said there was no evidence that the group successfully deployed an operational weapon, although it carried out a test launch of a guided rocket that appeared to fail. The company said safeguards blocked many requests but not all, while the group repeatedly tried to circumvent restrictions.The Yemen case was among several conventional-weapons operations identified by Anthropic, including work involving drone swarms, torpedo interception and targeting systems for electronic warfare and air-defence suppression. The company also identified around 35 potentially concerning biological research efforts over a 30-day period, while cautioning that it could not determine whether those activities were intended for harm or legitimate scientific research.The concerns are now extending to the highest levels of international security discussions. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is due to brief the UN Security Council on AI and international security next week, according to Reuters. The meeting comes as governments consider how increasingly powerful AI systems should be governed and how common safety standards could be established.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: BENGALURU: A UK-returned MTech graduate, who had recently joined an infrastructure company, has been arrested on charges of kidnapping and killing the.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A UK-returned MTech graduate, who had recently joined an infrastructure company, has been arrested on charges of kidnapping and killing the 13-year-old son of his former neighbour in Bengaluru Urban district on Wednesday night.Police said the accused, Wala Bhaskar Reddy, allegedly planned to extort Rs 1 crore from the boy’s realtor father to repay his family’s debts amounting to Rs 3 crore. His accomplice in the murder, identified as Edukondalu, is on the run.Based on preliminary investigations, police officers said the Reddys and the family of M Prajwal, a Class VIII student, were neighbours in Yelahanka before the latter moved to another lane in the locality. On Wednesday, Bhaskar allegedly picked up Prajwal near his house in his compact SUV, telling him they would buy firecrackers. He also promised to teach the boy how to drive.According to police, Bhaskar and Edukondalu drove Prajwal to an isolated spot, made a video of him in their custody and struck the boy on the head with a wooden log, leaving him unconscious.The accused then moved Prajwal to another deserted site and rained bricks on the boy, bludgeoning him to death. Police said the accused had planned to send Prajwal’s video, recorded before the killing, to his family and demand ransom.The duo stood on a compound wall and rained hollow bricks on the boy, bludgeoning him to death. Police said the accused had planned to send Prajwal’s video, recorded before killing him, to his family and demand ransom.“Edukondalu is a private school bus cleaner and agreed after money was offered. Following the boy’s death, he left the scene and Bhaskar decided to take Prajwal’s body to Nellore in Andhra Pradesh, and dispose it there,” police said. He wrapped the body in an abandoned and torn mattress found at the site and then placed it in the SUV’s boot.However, it was while transporting the body that Reddy’s plan began to unravel. Police said he was inebriated when he rammed the SUV into an electric pole. He continued driving, before crashing into two cars parked outside an apartment complex near Chikkajala.Hearing the impact, security personnel and residents rushed out and caught Reddy. Suspecting that he was drunk, they searched the vehicle and discovered the boy’s body in the boot.“Preliminary investigations revealed that the boy’s father, Manohar, and Bhaskar Reddy were neighbours for some years. There is no enmity between the two families, nor are they business rivals. The boy had a craze for cars and the accused took advantage of it and lured him,” said deputy commissioner of police (North East division) G K Mithun KumarPolice are questioning Bhaskar to determine other reasons he kidnapped and killed Prajwal. articles.body: US President Donald Trump will meet Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodriguez in New York on Tuesday, a senior US official said on Friday. This would mark the first in-person meeting between the two leaders since Washington removed former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January.The meeting will take place on the sidelines of a reception hosted by Trump for leaders attending the UN General Assembly, US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said during a briefing call. The talks are expected to bring Trump and Rodriguez together as Washington continues to engage with Venezuela over its energy sector."The president will host a UN General Assembly leaders' reception. Venezuela's communications ministry, which handles press queries for the government, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The meeting comes weeks after the US and Venezuela signed an energy agreement that would allow Washington to take partial control of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. The deal aims to revive the country's battered energy industry with the involvement of American companies.The development also comes as Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado faces uncertainty over when to return to the country and seek public support. Machado left Venezuela late last year to receive the Nobel Peace Prize after largely living in hiding following the disputed 2024 election.Machado had sought to build an alliance with Trump well before Maduro's removal. Since Maduro was ousted, however, Trump has repeatedly expressed support for Rodriguez.Who is Delcy Rodriguez?Rodriguez, Maduro's former deputy, became Venezuela's acting president after Washington removed Maduro in January. articles.title: A conservation group bought nearly 2,000 acres of South Carolina forest before development could reach it; the land has now been transferred to the US government and permanently added to Sumter National Forest
articles.summary: US News: In a quiet but decisive win for conservation, a 1,950-acre tract of South Carolina forest that once faced the threat of development has been permanent.
articles.body: In a quiet but decisive win for conservation, a 1,950-acre tract of South Carolina forest that once faced the threat of development has been permanently protected as part of Sumter National Forest. The Nature Conservancy purchased the land in 2023, held it while paperwork and funding were finalised, and has now transferred it to the US Forest Service, ensuring the upland hardwoods, wetlands and streams near Joanna in Laurens County remain open to the public for generations. The move, reported by multiple local outlets, adds a significant new block of protected habitat to the Enoree Ranger District and shields the area from the southward creep of development along the I-26 corridor.A landscape saved just in timeThe newly protected acreage sits in Laurens County, directly adjoining the unincorporated community of Joanna and bordering land that Laurens County is turning into an equestrian park. The property includes large stands of upland hardwood forest, pockets of wetlands and a network of streams that drain into the Enoree River, a tributary of the broader Saluda basin. These habitats support white-tailed deer, wild turkey, songbirds and a range of amphibians and reptiles that depend on intact forest and clean water.Officials with The Nature Conservancy say the purchase was driven by urgency as much as opportunity. As development continues to move south along the I-26 corridor, natural spaces in the Upstate are increasingly under pressure from new housing, commercial projects and infrastructure. The conservancy’s team moved quickly to take the property off the real estate market and managed it until the transfer to the Forest Service could be finalised, preventing the land from being subdivided or sold to private developers.How the deal came togetherThe 1,950-acre transfer traces back to a larger 2,281-acre purchase by The Nature Conservancy in 2023, acquired for about 6.47 million dollars according to local reporting. From that original tract, Laurens County bought a 335-acre parcel in late 2024 with plans to develop an equestrian park that will connect to the Palmetto Trail and Sumter National Forest. The remaining acreage has now been handed over to the US Forest Service to become part of the national forest system.The transaction builds on earlier conservation wins in the same area. In 2025, The Nature Conservancy helped secure the largest conservation easement in Laurens County history at Creekwood Farms, protecting another 2,000-acre tract next to Sumter National Forest through a donated easement valued at 2 million dollars. Together, these deals create a growing mosaic of protected lands that link public forest, county parks and privately held conservation easements into a larger network of open space.What the addition means for Sumter National ForestSumter National Forest is already a major public resource in the Upstate, with more than 170,000 acres spread across Newberry, Union, Chester, Laurens and Fairfield counties as part of the Enoree Ranger District. The new 1,950-acre block extends the forest further into Laurens County and strengthens its presence near Joanna, a community that has watched growth inch closer in recent years. Once the US Forest Service formally incorporates the property into the national forest system, it will be opened for public access under the same rules that govern the rest of Sumter.The land will be co-managed for wildlife by the US Forest Service and the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources under the state’s Wildlife Management Area program. That designation keeps the area open for public hunting and fishing, while also supporting hiking, birding and other low-impact recreation. Forest supervisors say they plan to improve public access over time, adding trails and parking areas that connect the new acreage to existing routes in the Enoree Ranger District.Why permanent protection mattersTurning the property into part of a national forest does more than keep trees standing. It locks in long-term protections that make it far harder for the land to be sold off, subdivided or converted to other uses. National forest status also brings federal resources for habitat management, invasive species control and trail maintenance, helping ensure the forest remains healthy and accessible.For local residents, the addition offers a tangible buffer against sprawl. As new housing and commercial development push outward from Greenville, Spartanburg and other growing cities, protected forests provide breathing room, cleaner water and places for people to escape into nature without driving for hours. The contiguous block of forest also helps wildlife move across the landscape, reducing the fragmentation that can isolate populations and weaken ecosystems.A model for future conservation in South CarolinaThe Joanna-area deal fits into a broader push to expand protected lands across the state. It supports South Carolina’s Ten Million Acres Initiative, launched by Governor Henry McMaster in 2024, which aims to conserve millions of acres of forests, wetlands and working lands through partnerships with nonprofits, agencies and private landowners. Similar efforts are underway in other parts of the state, including a recent 1,700-acre acquisition along the I-95 corridor that will eventually become a state-owned forest in the Lowcountry.Conservation groups and public agencies say the Sumter expansion shows how strategic purchases, easements and transfers can work together to protect large, connected landscapes before development reaches them. By acting early and holding land until permanent protections are in place, organisations like The Nature Conservancy can give public agencies time to secure funding and complete the legal steps needed to add new areas to national forests and state parks.For now, the most visible result is simple. Nearly 2,000 acres of South Carolina forest that might have become subdivisions or strip malls will instead remain forest, open to the public and permanently part of Sumter National Forest.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Hugs, kisses minutes before Indian-origin woman and her friend get killed by train in Manhattan: Report
articles.summary: US News: An Indian-origin woman may have jumped onto a New York City subway track in an attempt to rescue her friend after he ended up on the tracks, before bo.
articles.body: An Indian-origin woman may have jumped onto a New York City subway track in an attempt to rescue her friend after he ended up on the tracks, before both were fatally struck by an approaching train, according to a report by the New York Post citing law-enforcement sources.Malaika Chitre, 24, and her longtime friend Navam Kaul, also 24, were killed at the Spring Street subway station in Lower Manhattan at around 3.15am on Sunday. Both were recent graduates of Rutgers University and had recently begun their professional careers.According to the New York Post, Chitre and Kaul were seen hugging and kissing on the platform shortly before the incident. Kaul then appeared to lose his balance and fall onto the tracks, hitting his head, prompting Chitre to go down after him to help.Law-enforcement sources told the Post that it remained unclear whether Kaul fell or deliberately made his way onto the tracks. But investigators were examining the possibility that Chitre followed him in an attempt to pull him to safety.An incident report obtained by the New York Daily News said the train operator told supervisors that she saw Chitre and Kaul sitting on the tracks as a southbound No. 4 train entered the station. The operator attempted to stop the train but could not prevent the collision.The report said Chitre appeared to be laughing and pulling Kaul towards her when the train struck them. Video footage circulating on social media also appeared to show the pair sitting together on the tracks shortly before the train arrived.The train operator activated the emergency brake, but there was not enough time to stop, according to reports. About 100 passengers were later evacuated from the train.Investigators are also examining whether alcohol or drugs played a role and whether the pair may have been too impaired or disoriented to understand the danger. However, there has been no official finding that either was intoxicated.Suicide has also been considered, but investigators have not concluded that the deaths were intentional. The New York Post reported that no suicide note was found at the scene.Chitre, who was from South Brunswick, New Jersey, graduated from Rutgers with a degree in public health and was working as a quality operations specialist at Acadia Pharmaceuticals while pursuing a Doctor of Pharmacy degree at Temple University. Kaul, from Sayreville, graduated from Rutgers Business School with a degree in finance and worked as a financial data analyst at Bloomberg.The two were part of the same social circles and South Asian community around Rutgers and had remained close friends after graduating in 2024.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Elon Musk has once again made headlines with bold claims about his brain-chip company Neuralink. In a recent post shared on social media platform X, Musk described the company's newest experiment as a “wonderful surprise” and even added, “I love you,” in response to the breakthrough. The experiment showcased Neuralink’s ability to restore lost functions, reinforcing Musk’s earlier promise of what he calls “Jesus-level technologies.” Musk has repeatedly used the phrase “Jesus-level miracles” to describe Neuralink’s potential to help quadriplegics walk again, restore sight to the blind, and even enable advanced human perception. He argues that the technology could fundamentally transform medicine by bridging neurological gaps and offering life-changing capabilities once thought impossible.The 'beautiful surprise' from Elon Musk’s NeuralinkNeuralink recently shared a video of a clinical trial participant with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) using the company's N1 brain implant to communicate again — not just through generic text-to-speech, but through a synthetic voice built to sound like his own, from before his illness took his ability to speak. The emotional high point of the clip: the participant using the implant to tell his partner "I love you," in a voice that matched how he used to sound.Musk responded to the demo with a short but cute reaction, saying “I love you." Given the context, it appears to be less about any single new technical milestone and more about the deeply human moment the technology enabled — a person regaining not just the ability to speak, but to sound like himself while doing it.Neuralink's post came with the standard regulatory caveat that the device remains experimental, hasn't been cleared by the FDA or other regulators, and that one participant's results don't guarantee similar outcomes for others in future trials.The 'Jesus-level' comparisonThis isn't the first time Musk has reached for lofty language to describe Neuralink's ambitions. At the Samson International Smart Mobility Summit in Israel earlier this year, Musk described the company's broader goals — restoring control to tetraplegics and, eventually, restoring sight to people born blind — as "Jesus-level technologies." When the interviewer followed up by calling them miracles, Musk agreed, clarifying he meant "miracles of science" rather than anything supernatural.It's a comparison Musk has leaned on before. articles.title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Employees hid question papers in shoes, paid Rs 8,000 each
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employee.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employees paid Rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by Thane City police.The chargesheet, filed before a Bhiwandi court on Friday, names 18 accused, including alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, and lays out how investigators traced the leak from the printing press to those allegedly trying to sell the papers in Maharashtra. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding, police said.How the papers allegedly got outAccording to the chargesheet, the leak was traced to Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd, an Agra-based printing press tasked with producing the confidential TET examination material.Between June 15 and 17, two employees and a former staffer allegedly concealed folded question papers inside their shoe insoles while leaving the premises. Security guards frisked their clothes but allegedly did not check their footwear, allowing the papers to be taken outside, the chargesheet said.The state had prepared four separate sets of question papers for the two TET papers to maintain confidentiality and allow one set to be selected on examination day. Investigators allege that all four sets were nevertheless taken out of the press.The employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers, according to the chargesheet.Leak exposed a day before examThe racket came to light on June 27, a day before the TET was scheduled to be held. Deputy commissioner of Police Pavan Bansod received information that three men were allegedly trying to sell question papers to a Bhiwandi resident.Police then laid a trap using decoy personnel in Kongaon and detained the suspects, recovering four sets of question papers. Officials of the Maharashtra state council of examination later verified that the seized material matched the actual TET paper.The examination, scheduled for June 28, was subsequently postponed.Police have booked the accused under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy, along with Maharashtra laws dealing with examination malpractice. A special investigation team is probing the case.Investigators have identified Gupta, a former coaching-class teacher, as the alleged mastermind. Police said he had previously been implicated in another examination paper leak in Odisha.The chargesheet cites money trails, technical evidence and the recovery of an original question paper from the Bihar residence of a relative of Gupta as evidence in the alleged supply chain. Police said a supplementary chargesheet would be filed as the investigation continues.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
